summary: Timeboxed access for redaction-pattern verification on streaming KV cache slices
description: Issue overview: Security & Applied ML teams need a minimal, auditable dataset to verify that our automated redaction patterns correctly remove PII and other sensitive tokens from streaming responses that are reconstructed from KV cache slices. Objective: provide time-limited, access-controlled slices of streaming KV cache along with hashing metadata so the privacy team can run deterministic redaction tests without exposing full customer session mappings. Constraints: no raw session->customer_id mapping leaves the environment; access must be timeboxed, logged, and restricted to named reviewers. Proposed delivery is a sanitized S3 bucket containing tokenized slices plus a manifest of redaction checkpoints.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Identify candidate KV cache keys by query time window (2026-03-01T00:00:00Z - 2026-03-02T00:00:00Z) and heuristics: streaming sessions flagged 'streaming=true' and failed-redaction=false.
2) Extract minimal context window (prefix + 128 tokens of KV cache) and replace customer identifiers with deterministic salts (sha256 hashed with salt id).

3) Produce tokenized slices in a gzipped JSONL format with only token ids + metadata (no plaintext prompt where PII might appear), plus a redaction checkpoint file that marks where our pipeline would have redacted in the original stream.
4) Place artifacts into a pre-provisioned, access-controlled S3 path (s3://redwood-sec-prod/tmp/redaction-verif/INT-600321/) and grant temporary STS credentials to approved reviewers for 72 hours.
5) Reviewer runs redaction verification harness and produces a report containing diff of patterns matched, false positives, and false negatives.
